structure: Part 15, Address book: list, view, edit and delete (GB-notification-service at 04a073b, read from the extracted copy in the work folder). Read in full: app/views/address-book.html (the list; DR2.1 sets isDesignRelease2Version so its DR2 branch applies: collapsible filter, category tabs, per-category table columns), app/views/address-book-view.html (one address as a summary list with Edit and Delete), app/views/address-book-lookup.html in edit mode (search and manual toggle hidden, manual fields shown, Save changes / Cancel), app/views/partials/address-book-manual-address-fields.html (the nine manual fields), app/views/design-release-2.1/delete-address.html with partials/design-release-2.1/delete-confirmation.html (the delete question), app/data/address-book.js (type labels, the four categories, seeded addresses, page size 8, per-category minimum counts) and app/data/address-book-address-types.js (the seven types and their hints). In app/routes.js: lines 6161-6265 (delete summary row and address HTML), 7052-7084 (DR2.1 base path), 9124-9729 (hrefs, pagination, results text, type filter items, merged address list, return paths, viewable addresses, view summary rows, view and delete render, update and delete of an entry, renderAddressBookEditPage, updated and deleted banner text, entry built from manual fields), 9944-10051 (getAddressBookViewModel, renderAddressBookPage, category aliases, base path), 10412-10523 (country items, body parsing and validation for the manual fields, reached by the edit POST), 11742-11745 (GET /address-book) and 11978-12044 (GET and POST edit, GET and POST delete, GET view). Covered: the list route, heading, intro, add button, filter (search and type), four category tabs, results text, both table layouts, View link, pagination, success banner and the empty state; the view page rows and actions; the edit page fields, labels, hint, seven validation messages and where save and cancel lead; the delete page row, copy, buttons and redirects; the seeded data and address types. The client-side search module (app-address-book-search) and the seed files consignment-addresses.js, contact-addresses.js and transporters.js are outside this part's read list; only what the list shows of them is claimed. Adding an address (/address-book/add) is part 16's.

claims.statement: The address book list is served at GET /address-book, which under Design Release 2.1 is mounted at /design-release-2.1/address-book.
The service navigation links to the address book at /design-release-2.1/address-book in Design Release 2.1, and the list page's form and add button use that path.
The address book list page shows an Alpha phase banner with a feedback link.
claims.quote: html: 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.'

claims.statement: The address book list page's heading is "Address book".
Under Design Release 2 and 2.1 the list page's intro, in large body text, reads "Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications".
claims.quote: Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications

claims.statement: The list page has an "Add a new address" button linking to the address book path followed by /add.
claims.quote:
text: "Add a new address",
      href: (serviceNavAddressBookHref if serviceNavAddressBookHref else "/address-book") + "/add"

claims.statement: When a success message is waiting in the session, the list page shows it in a success notification banner titled "Success", then clears it so it shows only once.
Under Design Release 2 and 2.1 the filter sits inside a collapsible details element whose summary reads "Filter addresses" with a chevron icon.
The filter is a GET form to the address book path, so search, type and category are carried as query parameters.
claims.quote: <form method="get" action="{{ serviceNavAddressBookHref if serviceNavAddressBookHref else '/address-book' }}" class="app-address-book-page__filter">

claims.statement: The filter form carries the selected category tab as a hidden field, so filtering stays on the current tab.
The filter has a search field labelled "Search", named search, with the placeholder "Search by name, address or country", prefilled with the current search.
claims.quote:
placeholder="Search by name, address or country"
                    value="{{ searchQuery or '' }}"

claims.statement: The search field has an icon button with the accessible name "Search"; it is type="button", so it does not submit the form itself, and the list is searched by the client-side app-address-book-search module, which the page gives every address book entry as JSON.
claims.note: The client-side module's script is outside this part's read list; what it does with the JSON is not read here.

claims.statement: The filter has a select labelled "Type", named type, whose first option is "Select one" with an empty value.
On the Transporter tab the Type filter offers only "Commercial" and "Private" after "Select one".
On the other tabs the Type filter offers only the address types that belong to that tab's category, drawn from the address-type list (which has no divider entry).

So the Origin and Consignor tab's Type filter offers "Place of Origin" and "Consignor"; the Destination, Consignee and Importer tab offers "Consignee", "Importer" and "Place of Destination"; the Branch tab offers "Branch Address". The category's other types (consignor-or-exporter, exporter, contact, packer) have no filter option.
claims.note: Derived by intersecting each category's types with the address-type options list.

claims.statement: The type filter matches a transporter by its type label (Commercial or Private) and any other address when any of its types equals the selected type.
Search is a case-insensitive substring match of the trimmed search text against each address's search text.
An address's search text covers its name, type labels, address, approval number and country.
claims.quote:
searchText: buildSearchText([
      address.name,
      displayTypeLabel,
      ...typeLabels,
      formattedAddress,
      address.approvalNumber,
      address.country
    ])

claims.statement: A transporter's search text covers its name, type label (Commercial or Private), address and approval number.
claims.quote:
searchText: buildSearchText([
      transporter.name,
      typeLabel,
      transporter.address,
      transporter.approvalNumber
    ])

claims.statement: An edited or added address's search text covers its name, type label, formatted address and country.
claims.quote:
searchText: buildAddressBookSearchText([
      manualAddress.nameOrOrganisation,
      typeLabel,
      formattedAddress,
      manualAddress.country
    ])

claims.statement: Under Design Release 2 and 2.1 the list is split into four category tabs, in this order: "Origin and Consignor", "Destination, Consignee and Importer", "Transporter" and "Branch".
Each tab panel has its own heading: "Origin and Consignor addresses", "Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses", "Transporter addresses" or "Branch addresses".

The Origin and Consignor category holds the place-of-origin, consignor, consignor-or-exporter and exporter types; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place-of-destination, contact and packer; Transporter holds transporter; Branch holds branch-address.
The selected tab comes from the category query parameter; when it is missing or unknown the Origin and Consignor tab is shown.
The older category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are accepted as aliases of origin-and-consignor and destination-consignee-importer.
An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types, so an address with several types can appear on more than one tab.
Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the type filter.
Above the table, a results line reads "Showing <start>-<end> of <total>", or "Showing 0 of 0" when nothing matches.
On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, followed by an action column with the visually hidden header "Action".
claims.quote:
<th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header app-address-book-table__header">Type</th>
                      <th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header app-address-book-table__header">Address</th>
                      <th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header app-address-book-table__header">Country</th>

claims.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, followed by the action column.
In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest.
In the Address column each address line is shown on its own line, ending in a comma except the last.
In the Type column an address with several types shows their labels joined by a comma and space.

The list shows type labels "Place of origin", "Consignor" (for consignor, consignor-or-exporter and exporter), "Consignee", "Importer", "Place of destination", "Transporter", "Branch", "Contact address" and "Packer"; these differ in case and wording from the filter options ("Place of Origin", "Branch Address").
claims.quote:
'place-of-origin': 'Place of origin',
  consignor: 'Consignor',
  'consignor-or-exporter': 'Consignor',
  consignee: 'Consignee',
  importer: 'Importer',
  'place-of-destination': 'Place of destination',
  transporter: 'Transporter',
  'branch-address': 'Branch',
  contact: 'Contact address',
  exporter: 'Consignor',
  packer: 'Packer'

claims.statement: A transporter's Type is its own type, Commercial or Private, defaulting to Commercial; its Country is taken as the last comma-separated part of its address.
Each row ends with a "View" link to that address's view page.
The list shows 8 addresses per page.
When there is more than one page, pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, plus "Previous" and "Next" links where they apply.
Pagination links keep the category, search and type filter and add page only for pages after the first.
A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page.
When no address matches, the list shows an empty table and "Showing 0 of 0", with no empty-state message or prompt to add an address.
claims.note: No empty-state copy exists in the template; inferred from the table rendering zero rows.

claims.statement: The list shows addresses the user added this session first, then the seeded addresses less any deleted this session, each with any edits made this session applied.
Additions, edits and deletions in the address book are held in the user's prototype session only, not saved anywhere else.
claims.note: Prototype persistence; the real service is expected to persist to the address-book service. Inferred from every write going to req.session.data.

claims.statement: The address view page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId.
The view page can show any address the service knows by id, searching the address book first and then consignment addresses, contact addresses and transporters.
If no address has that id, the view page redirects to its back link: the return path, or the address book list.
The view page has a "Back" link to the return query path when one is given, otherwise to the address book list.

A return path is honoured only when it starts with a single /; anything else falls back to the default, and an unversioned /address-book path is rewritten to the Design Release's own address book path.
The view page's heading is the address's name.
The view page's summary list always shows the rows "Name or organisation name", "Address line 1", "Town or city", "Postcode or Zip code", "Country", "Email address" and "Phone number".
The view page shows "Address line 2 (optional)" after Address line 1 and "County (optional)" after Town or city only when they have a value.
The view page's row values come from the address's stored details or, failing those, are split from its address lines into the manual fields.

When the address is in the address book, the view page shows a secondary "Edit" button and a warning "Delete" button; an address found only elsewhere (a consignment, contact or transporter address) shows neither.
The Edit button links to <address book>/<id>/edit and the Delete button to <address book>/<id>/delete, each carrying the view page's return path when it is not the list itself.
The edit page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId/edit; if the id is not in the address book it redirects to the return path or the list.
The edit page's heading is "Edit address and contact details".
The edit page's "Back" link goes to the return path when given, otherwise to the address's view page.
In edit mode the address search and the "Enter address manually" link are hidden and the manual address fields are shown straight away.
The edit page is prefilled with the address's current details.
The address type cannot be changed on the edit page: it is posted as a hidden field, and the type select items the handler builds are not rendered.
claims.note: addressTypeItems and addressTypeLabel are passed to the view but address-book-lookup.html never uses them.

claims.statement: The edit form's fields sit under a section heading "Address": "Name or organisation name", "Address line 1", "Address line 2 (optional)", "Town or city", "County (optional)", "Postcode or Zip code" and a "Country" select.
Below them, under a section heading "Contact details", the edit form has "Email address" and "Phone number".
The "Phone number" field has the hint "For international numbers include the country code".
claims.quote: text: "For international numbers include the country code"

claims.statement: The Country select lists United Kingdom with the service's country options, sorted alphabetically, with no blank "Select" option, and the address's country selected.
claims.quote:
const options = [
    { value: 'United Kingdom', label: 'United Kingdom' },
    ...countryOptions
  ].sort((left, right) => left.label.localeCompare(right.label))

claims.statement: The edit page's buttons are "Save changes" and a secondary "Cancel".
claims.quote: text: "Save changes" if isEditMode else "Save and continue",

claims.statement: The edit form posts to <address book>/<id>/edit, carrying the return path when it is not the list.
Cancel on the edit page clears any errors and returns to the return path, by default the address's view page, without saving.
Posting the edit form for an id that is not in the address book redirects to the return path or the list without saving.
Every edit field is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is validated and saved.
If "Name or organisation name" is empty, the error is "Enter a name or organisation name".
claims.quote: addError('addressBookManualName', 'Enter a name or organisation name', '#address-book-manual-name')

claims.statement: If "Address line 1" is empty, the error is "Enter address line 1".
If "Town or city" is empty, the error is "Enter a town or city".
If "Postcode or Zip code" is empty, the error is "Enter a postcode or Zip code".
claims.quote: addError('addressBookManualPostcode', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', '#address-book-manual-postcode')

claims.statement: If "Country" is empty, the error is "Select a country".
If "Email address" is empty, the error is "Enter an email address".
If "Phone number" is empty, the error is "Enter a phone number".
"Address line 2 (optional)" and "County (optional)" are not validated and may be left blank.
claims.note: validateAddressBookManualAddress has no check for addressLine2 or county.

claims.statement: The source checks only that each required field is filled; it sets no format rule or message for email address, phone number or postcode, and no maximum lengths.
claims.note: Looked in validateAddressBookManualAddress; only presence checks exist.

claims.statement: On a validation error the edit page is shown again with an error summary titled "There is a problem", each error linked to its field, the message shown on the field, and the values the user entered kept.
When the edit is valid it replaces the address's details, keeps its primary address type, and returns the user to the address book list (its default tab), not the view page.
Editing an address with several types saves it with only its first type, so it loses its other types.
claims.note: entry.type is the primary type only; buildAddressBookEntryFromManual then sets types to that one value. Looks like a prototype defect, recorded as observed.

claims.statement: After a valid edit the list shows a success banner reading "<Name> address updated", with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, or "Address updated" when the name is blank.
An edited address's formatted address joins address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode with commas, leaving out blanks; the country is kept separately.

For a seeded address, an edit is merged over the original without replacing its stored address lines, so the list's Address column and the delete page can still show the old address lines after an edit.
claims.note: buildAddressBookEntryFromManual sets address but not addressLines; the template prefers addressLines. Prototype defect, recorded as observed.

claims.statement: The delete page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId/delete; if the id is not in the address book it redirects to the return path or the list.
Design Release 2.1 overrides the delete-address view with its own, which uses the journey layout and an Alpha phase banner.
The delete page's heading is "Delete this address?".

The delete page shows a summary list with one row, "Address", holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, leaving out any line that repeats one already shown (ignoring case).
When the address has no name, lines or country, the delete page's Address row falls back to its manual-field details, and failing those shows "Not applicable".
Below the summary the delete page says "Confirm that you want to delete this address." and "This action cannot be undone."
The delete page has a warning button "Yes, delete" that posts to <address book>/<id>/delete, carrying the return path when it is not the list.
The delete page has a "No, cancel" link and a "Back" link, both to the address's view page with the return path carried on.
Confirming the delete removes the address from the address book: an address added this session is removed outright, and a seeded address is recorded as deleted and any edit to it discarded.
After a delete the list shows a success banner reading "<Name> address deleted", with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, or "Address deleted" when the name is blank.
After a delete the user goes to the return path, unless that path is the deleted address's own pages, in which case they go to the address book list.
Posting a delete for an id that is not in the address book changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
The source gives the delete action no extra check, such as whether the address is in use on a notification.
claims.note: Looked at the POST delete handler and deleteAddressBookEntry; nothing considers notifications that use the address.

claims.statement: The seeded address book is built from the service's consignment addresses, contact addresses (typed "Contact address"), transporters, six multi-type addresses and eight template addresses.
Each seeded address's id is its source id followed by a hyphen and its position, and its view link is /address-book/<id>.

The seeded multi-type addresses are Green Valley Farm (place of origin, consignor), Alpine Breeding Centre, Austria (place of origin, consignor-or-exporter), Nordic Livestock Export AB, Sweden (consignor, place of origin), Northern Livestock Imports Ltd (consignee, importer), Britannia Trade & Livestock Ltd (consignee, importer, place of destination) and Riverside Holding Facility (place of destination, consignee).

The seeded template addresses, all in the United Kingdom with email and phone, are Acorn Farm (importer), Green Valley Farm (place of origin), Northern Livestock Exports (consignor), Britannia Trade Livestock (consignee), West Coast Animal Imports (place of destination) and three branches: Defra Liverpool Branch, Defra Manchester Branch and Defra Birmingham Branch.

The seed pads each category with copies of template addresses until it holds at least 16 Origin and Consignor, 16 Destination, Consignee and Importer, 8 Transporter and 3 Branch addresses, so the first two tabs paginate.

The seeded transporters, typed Commercial or Private, are Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd, Danish Meat Export ApS and Portuguese Livestock Lda (Commercial), and Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, Romanian Agri Exports SRL, Slovak Farm Export and Finnish Livestock Oy (Private).
claims.note: transporters.js is outside this part's read list; only names and types were listed to show what the Transporter tab holds.

claims.statement: Every view, edit and delete page sets the service navigation's active item to the address book.
